newsitem.title: MEXICO: Veteran Mexican union boss leaves hospital.
newsitem.headline: Veteran Mexican union boss leaves hospital.

text.p: Veteran Mexican union boss Fidel Velazquez left hospital on Saturday after a four-day stay to treat an attack of pneumonia, the official news agency Notimex reported.
Notimex said that Velazquez, who has been a reliable union ally for the government for more than half a century, left hospital "in good shape and on his own two feet".

The 96-year-old president of the Confederation of Mexican Workers (CTM) would complete his recovery at home and rest for a week before returning to work, his personal physician Salomon Jasqui told Notimex.
The government is eagerly counting on Velazquez's support during the annual round of negotiations over next year's economic plan, which is due to be agreed by mid-November.

Velazquez, one of the few living survivors of the 1910-17 Mexican Revolution still to hold high office, has been in hospital four times this year. He was treated for pneumonia in April and later had two separate operations to remove eye cataracts.
